title: The eager DOC open stops decoding text four times, resolving each PAPX three times, and copying the WordDocument stream twice
code_state: crates/litchi-doc only: parts/text.rs, parts/pap_bin_table.rs, parts/pap/parser.rs, parts/fib.rs, parts/glossary.rs, document/package.rs, document/model/state.rs
implements: items DOC-2, DOC-3 and DOC-4 (rank 11) of change 0587
reason_codes: every step is value-identical by construction: a const transcription of the existing Windows-1252 match, a fused decode that is from_utf16_lossy and the old cp_to_byte builder in one pass, reuse of a parse of the same bytes, a pure-function style baseline cache, and a shared view of the WordDocument stream that keeps FileInformationBlock::raw_data byte for byte

a differential digest over all 57 .doc fixtures is byte-identical on both legs: text, every paragraph's resolved properties and runs, paragraph counts, section table, subdocument ranges, FIB bytes, and the exact Debug text of all 15 refusals

deterministic counts move the way the mechanism predicts: per-open instructions -20.11%, -11.27% and -18.36% on three real fixtures; parse_sprms calls per PAPX entry 3.08 to 1.10, 2.03 to 1.12 and 2.03 to 1.19; FileInformationBlock::parse_at's 698,280 Ir per open of the 1.6 MB fixture removed entirely

DOC-4 was implemented as a shared offset view rather than as the truncation the survey suggested, because the audit found public readers of raw_data (smart_tags::Snapshot::fib_bytes, its finish() and its fingerprint()) and validators comparing against raw_data().len(); truncation would move a refusal and change a public byte sequence, so it is left to a frozen design record

accepted_evidence.instruction_counts: callgrind isolation pairs (s=10 against s=110, divided by 100) on the eager Package::document() open of three real fixtures, both legs, using change 0587's retained docppt-survey driver rebuilt against each checkout
accepted_evidence.isolated_read_counts: isolation pairs (s=100 against s=1100, divided by 1000) for Document::paragraph_count(), Document::text() and FileInformationBlock::get_all_subdoc_ranges() with the document opened once outside the loop
accepted_evidence.native_cycles: perf stat, three runs per leg, 20 warmups plus 2,000 timed opens each, on all three fixtures; and 50 warmups plus 2,000 paragraph_count calls each on saved-by-table.doc
accepted_evidence.paired_timing: tools/perf-baseline, four windows, legs ordered A1 B1 B2 A2 with an A/A floor A3 against A4 in the same window, 400 to 500 samples per leg pooled to 800 or 1,000 per state, CPU 16 pinned; windows 1 and 2 measure a superseded candidate and are retained as the regression evidence, windows 3 and 4 measure the committed code
accepted_evidence.differential_oracle: a probe over every .doc fixture in the tree comparing decoded text, every resolved paragraph and its runs, paragraph counts, sections, subdocument ranges, FIB bytes and refusal text; outputs byte-identical
accepted_evidence.unit_tests: cargo test -p litchi-doc, 996 lib tests plus 41 suites, with new tests for the Windows-1252 table over all 256 bytes, the fused decode against the old two-step form over seven inputs including lone surrogates, ANSI and Unicode piece decoding, and the style-baseline cache's bound and eviction
accepted_evidence.writer_output: doc_semantic_noop_edit_save and doc_semantic_one_edit_save verify exact no-op bytes, deterministic changed bytes, public reopen, forward patch and inverse restoration outside timing; 1,000 samples per state per window with no verification failure

accepted_costs.layout_sensitivity: the first candidate build was 13% to 15% worse at p50 on doc_semantic_paragraph_count in two independent windows against a floor under 0.3%, while the query's own instruction count moved by +0.03% and its native cycles by -0.66%; a ninety-instruction edit to get_all_subdoc_ranges turned it into -2.63% and -0.32%, so at these scenario sizes the harness percentiles rank candidates rather than measure them
accepted_costs.host_contention: seven other agents built and measured on the same host throughout; the A/A floor reached -10.26% at p50 on doc_semantic_open/large in window 1 and -80% at p95 in window 4, so means and tails of windows 2 and 4 are contaminated and p50 is the metric read
accepted_costs.harness_corpora: the timed corpora are generated by the DOC writer and are not the fixtures the callgrind and perf stat legs use; the two are never combined in one figure
accepted_costs.instruction_counts_rank_work: callgrind counts rep movsb per byte, so the copy removals are also priced natively
accepted_costs.two_binaries: every timing comparison is between two differently linked binaries; no attempt was made to control code layout

known_gaps.not_measured: cold page cache, peak RSS, allocation profiles, non-Linux or non-x86-64 targets
known_gaps.not_exercised: the encrypted path beyond the two PasswordRequired fixtures, which refuse before the FIB is reparsed; and the attached glossary FIB, since no fixture in the corpus has pnNext != 0, so DOC-4's second copy removal is reasoned from the source rather than observed
known_gaps.unexplained: FloatingPictures.doc does 5.70% fewer instructions and 1.97% more native cycles per open; doc_semantic_open/large moves +1.47% and -7.69% at p50 across windows 3 and 4 against floors of -2.4% and -2.5%
known_gaps.left_on_the_table: cp_to_byte is still eight bytes per UTF-16 code unit and still built eagerly (38.3% of the saved-by-table.doc open after this change); the per-entry [sprms, piece_modifier].concat() still allocates once per PAPX entry because the result is retained in the run; TapParser still reparses the same grpprl for table paragraphs; truncating the FIB to its declared extent needs its own design record

withheld: any registered speedup, cold-cache, physical-device, peak-RSS, allocation-profile, concurrency-scaling or cross-platform result

provenance.host: AMD EPYC 9R45, 32 cores, 123 GiB, Linux 7.0.0-1012-aws, rustc 1.95.0, valgrind 3.26.0, CPU 16 pinned with taskset
